reason: Follow the only available action to start developing muscle cells.
expectation: The signals should guide some stem-cell descendants toward muscle precursors, though the intermediate stage is uncertain.

effect: The signals produced myoblasts, which can now fuse into muscle fibres.
reaction: The label makes the precursor stage clear.
reason: Use the only offered combination to fuse the aligned myoblasts.
expectation: The fusion proteins should join the cells into a multinucleated muscle fibre.

effect: The myoblasts fused into multinucleated fibres with space for pulling machinery.
reaction: The retained nuclei make the fusion clear.
reason: Add the filament units using the only offered combination to equip the fibres for pulling.
expectation: Actin and myosin will become organized inside the fibres, though a calcium signal may still be needed to trigger a pull.

effect: The fibre now has organized filaments and reset myosin heads, but actin's grip sites remain covered.
reaction: The inset clarifies why the fibre is not pulling yet.
reason: Use the only offered combination to trigger the filament machinery.
expectation: Calcium should expose actin's grip sites so myosin can attach and generate a pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing ATP-dependent myosin cycling and filament sliding; the fibre now needs to reset.
reaction: The distinction between sliding filaments and shortening filaments is clear and useful.
reason: Use the only offered combination to remove calcium and prepare the fibre to relax.
expectation: The membranes will use ATP to pump calcium back into storage, allowing the grip sites to be covered again.

effect: Calcium pumping stopped the pull and reset the fibre; the next goal is to build and attach both elbow muscles.
reaction: The outside pull needed to lengthen the relaxed fibre is a useful distinction.
reason: Use the only offered combination to begin incorporating connective material into the muscle.
expectation: The matrix may support or bundle the muscle fibres in preparation for adding tendons.

effect: The matrix now surrounds individual fibres and bundles them into fascicles, with enough bundles for both muscles.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre membrane and its connective layer is helpful.
reason: Start building the biceps from the fascicles and its sheaths and tendons.
expectation: The fascicles should fill the biceps muscle-head spaces and connect with its tendon structures.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs building, but either muscle seems a reasonable starting point.

effect: The biceps now has two filled muscle heads and tendons that transmit force through connective tissue.
reaction: The force-path inset connects the fibre bundles to the tendon clearly.
reason: Build the triceps as well before attaching the muscles to the skeleton.
expectation: The fascicles should fill the triceps heads and connect to its tendon structures.

alternatives.reason: Attaching the completed biceps is also useful, but I want to build both muscles first.

effect: Both muscles are built; their tendons still need attaching to the skeleton.
reaction: The three triceps heads and common tendon make its structure clear.
reason: Attach the biceps first to start connecting the muscles across the elbow.
expectation: The biceps tendons should attach near the shoulder and radius, positioning it to bend the elbow.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attaching, but either seems a reasonable place to start.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow and can flex it; the extensor slot remains empty.
reaction: The two poses make the biceps' effect on the elbow clear.
reason: Use the only offered combination to attach the triceps and fill the extensor slot.
expectation: The triceps should attach across the elbow and pull to extend it, opposing the biceps.

effect: The triceps fills the extensor slot, completing the arm assembly and showing how its attachment produces the opposite movement to the biceps.
reaction: The paired attachment diagrams make the contrast between flexion and extension clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered contraction was most worthwhile: the planned cycle connects ATP use to myosin movement and distinguishes filament sliding from filament shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the two muscles was somewhat repetitive: both results use the same force-path inset, although their head counts and tendon routes differ.

surprise.text: Relaxation also requires ATP to pump calcium back into storage, and the fibre lengthens under an outside pull rather than actively pushing itself longer.

arbitrary.text: The order of building and attaching biceps versus triceps felt arbitrary, though both actions had clear purposes. Most other steps offered only one combination, limiting meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue: the planned illustrations connect molecular machinery to movement at a joint, though I would hope for more meaningful choices than the mostly single-option sequence here.
